blocks.x: New York City is an explosion of arts and culture, from its world-class museums and live music venues to the countless ways art finds its way into everyday life. And this November, the city’s vibrant art scene is coming together for something entirely new.

For the first time ever, New York City is getting its own Art Week, a four-day celebration bringing together galleries, cultural institutions, artists, and art lovers across the five boroughs’ wider creative landscape. Taking place from November 11–14, 2026, Art Week NYC will spotlight the city’s contemporary art scene through exhibitions, gallery openings, conversations, performances, and special programming.

The inaugural event will unfold across some of Manhattan’s most recognizable art destinations, including Chelsea, the Upper East Side, the Lower East Side, and Tribeca. Each neighborhood has its own artistic identity, offering visitors the chance to discover everything from established galleries and cutting-edge contemporary work to intimate cultural spaces and unexpected creative discoveries.

Source / The New Museum
What to Expect: NYC’s Inaugural Art Week

Presented by Penske Media Corporation (PMC) in partnership with flagship art publications Artforum, ARTnews, and Art in America, Art Week NYC is designed to unify the city’s vast creative landscape. Rather than restricting the art world to a single fair tent, the initiative turns the city itself into the venue.

80+ Participating Galleries: Major commercial powerhouses and emerging project spaces across four core districts (Chelsea, Tribeca, Lower East Side, and Upper East Side) will open their doors simultaneously. Expect synchronized late-night openings, artist walkthroughs, and curated solo or group exhibitions.

32 Cultural Institutions & Nonprofits: Leading museums—including the New Museum, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Guggenheim—alongside civic spaces like MTA Arts & Design and High Line Art, will anchor the week with dedicated public access and special installations.

Central Midtown Hub: Hosted in partnership with ARTnews and Art in America, a dedicated Midtown venue will serve as a central meeting ground for panels, live journalism, sponsor activations, and speaker series.

Cross-Disciplinary Activations: Programming throughout the four days will highlight where fine art intersects with adjacent creative fields, including film, fashion, music, architecture, and technology.

Art Wage r/ Getty Images
The Programming to Look Out For
Whether you want to drop in for a quick panel or build a full multi-day gallery crawl, Art Week NYC features four core programming tracks:

DISCOVER: Coordinated Gallery Openings & Events
Facilitated by Artforum, over 70 gallery events will roll out across the major gallery districts. Keep an eye out for live performances (such as Lee Kun-Yong’s performance at Pace Gallery), curator-led tours, and evening receptions tailored to neighborhood schedules.

ENGAGE: The New Museum Symposium
As Art Week’s lead institutional partner, the New Museum on the Lower East Side will host a full-day public symposium. Co-hosted with Artforum, the schedule features five major panel discussions uniting influential artists, curators, and cultural critics to discuss art in the modern urban landscape.

EXPLORE: Curated Neighborhood Walking Tours
Guided walking itineraries will run daily through Chelsea, Tribeca, the Upper East Side, and the Lower East Side. These walks connect viewers to gallery highlights, public art installations, historical neighborhood landmarks, and localized dining spots.

LEARN: ARTnews Industry Panels
Helmed by editors from ARTnews and Art in America, these sessions tackle pressing issues impacting the contemporary market—covering topics from institutional patronage and artist estates to collector trends and public funding.

Source / Art Week NYC
How to Participate
Art Week NYC is open to art professionals, seasoned collectors, and curious newcomers alike. Here is how to plan your experience:

Explore by Neighborhood: Map out your visits geographically to make the most of your time. Focus on Tribeca and the Lower East Side for cutting-edge contemporary work, or Chelsea and the Upper East Side for grand-scale solo presentations and historic surveys.

Reserve Tickets & Walkthroughs: While many gallery walk-ins and outdoor installations are free to the public, institutional programs, panel discussions at the New Museum, and guided walking tours require advance registration.
Leverage Digital Guides: Download the Bloomberg Connects app (the official digital partner) to access event maps, self-guided audio tours, and exhibition guides directly on your phone.
Sign Up for Updates: Visit the official portal at art-week.com to subscribe to the newsletter for early-access event tickets, complete speaker lists, and the finalized neighborhood schedule.
For more details, see Art Week’s official website.
